title: Garlic Egg Fried Rice
description: A comforting, fragrant Filipino-inspired sinangag upgraded with fluffy scrambled eggs and umami soy glaze.

substitutions.soy sauce: Use liquid seasoning (Knorr/Maggi) or a pinch of salt + Worcestershire sauce.
substitutions.rice: Day-old cold rice works best; if using freshly cooked rice, spread it on a plate for 10 mins to cool.

steps: Mince 4-5 cloves of garlic finely. Whisk 2 eggs in a small bowl with a pinch of salt.
Heat 2 tbsp cooking oil in a wok or wide skillet over medium heat. Fry the minced garlic until golden and fragrant (reserve half for garnish if desired).
Push garlic to the side, pour in the beaten eggs, and scramble until just set.
Add 2 cups of cold leftover rice, breaking up any clumps with your spatula.
Drizzle 1.5 tbsp soy sauce around the edges of the pan and toss over high heat for 2-3 minutes until smoky and evenly coated.

title: Classic Soy-Vinegar Adobo
description: Savory, tangy, and rich braised chicken or pork simmered in soy sauce, vinegar, crushed garlic, and bay leaves.

substitutions.chicken: Works identically with pork belly, tofu cubes, or hard-boiled eggs.
substitutions.vinegar: Cane vinegar (Datu Puti) is traditional, but apple cider or white vinegar works great.

steps: Combine 500g chicken pieces, 1/3 cup soy sauce, 5 cloves crushed garlic, and black pepper in a bowl. Marinate for at least 15 minutes.
Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pot over medium-high heat. Sear the chicken pieces (reserving the marinade) until lightly browned on both sides.
Pour in the reserved marinade, 1/2 cup water, and bay leaves. Bring to a boil, then lower heat and simmer covered for 20 minutes.
Pour in 1/4 cup vinegar. Do NOT stir for the first 3 minutes so the raw acid cooks off cleanly.
Simmer uncovered for another 8-10 minutes until the sauce reduces to a glossy glaze. Serve hot with steamed rice.

title: Tortang Talong (Grilled Eggplant Omelette)
description: Smoky blistered eggplant flattened into a fan and pan-fried inside a golden, crispy-edged egg batter.

substitutions.eggplant: No open flame to char? Microwave pricked eggplants for 4-5 mins until soft, then peel.

steps: Char 2 whole Asian eggplants directly over a gas burner or under a broiler for 6-8 minutes until skin is blackened and flesh is tender.
Let cool slightly, then gently peel away the charred skin while keeping the stem intact.
Place each peeled eggplant on a plate and press flat with a fork to create a wide fan shape.
Beat 2-3 eggs in a shallow bowl with salt and pepper. Dip each flattened eggplant into the egg mixture until well coated.
Fry in a skillet with 2 tbsp hot oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side until golden brown. Serve with banana ketchup or spiced vinegar.

title: Ginisang Sardinas with Egg & Garlic
description: A student and weeknight lifesaver: canned sardines in tomato sauce elevated with sautéed aromatics and silky egg ribbons.

substitutions.canned sardines: Canned mackerel or tuna in oil/tomato sauce can be used in the exact same way.

steps: Heat 1 tbsp oil in a pan. Sauté sliced onion and minced garlic until softened and fragrant.
Pour in 1 can of sardines in tomato sauce along with 1/4 cup water. Simmer gently for 3 minutes.
Lightly beat 1-2 eggs and slowly drizzle into the simmering tomato broth while stirring gently to create silky ribbons.
Season with black pepper and serve immediately over hot rice.

title: 15-Minute Garlic Butter & Egg Pasta
description: Silky, restaurant-style emulsified pasta made entirely from pantry staples without needing heavy cream.

substitutions.butter: Use olive oil or regular cooking oil with a pinch of extra salt.
substitutions.cheese: Grated cheddar, quickmelt, or parmesan all work—just temper off the heat.

steps: Boil 200g pasta in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 1/2 cup of starchy pasta cooking water before draining.
In a separate bowl, whisk 2 egg yolks (or 1 whole egg) with grated cheese and plenty of black pepper.
Melt 2 tbsp butter in a skillet over low heat and gently sauté 4 cloves thinly sliced garlic until golden.
Remove skillet from heat! Add drained hot pasta and a splash of reserved pasta water, tossing quickly.
Pour in the egg mixture while tossing continuously off-heat so the residual warmth creates a glossy, creamy sauce without scrambling.

title: Ginisang Monggo (Savory Mung Bean Stew)
description: Protein-packed, earthy mung bean stew simmered with garlic, onions, tomatoes, and leafy greens.

substitutions.spinach: Use malunggay leaves, ampalaya (bitter melon) leaves, or chopped bok choy.
substitutions.fish sauce: Season with salt or soy sauce if patis isn't in your pantry.

steps: Rinse 1 cup dried mung beans. Boil in 4 cups water for 30-35 minutes until beans split and soften into a creamy mash.
In a separate pot, heat 1 tbsp oil and sauté minced garlic, chopped onion, and diced tomato until tomatoes break down.
Pour the cooked mung beans and their broth into the aromatics pot. Stir well and simmer for 5 minutes.
Season with fish sauce or salt to taste, then fold in fresh spinach or leafy greens for 1 minute until wilted.

title: Crispy Tofu & Soy-Calamansi Sisig
description: Golden pan-fried tofu cubes tossed in a zesty, savory onion, chili, and soy-citrus dressing.

substitutions.calamansi: Use lemon juice, lime juice, or a splash of white vinegar for brightness.
substitutions.mayonnaise: Optional for creaminess—skip it for a lighter, tangy soy-garlic glaze.

steps: Pat 300g firm tofu dry with paper towels and cut into small 1/2-inch cubes.
Pan-fry tofu cubes in hot oil over medium-high heat for 8-10 minutes until golden and crispy on all sides. Drain excess oil.
In the same pan, sauté finely diced red onion, minced garlic, and chopped chili for 1 minute until fragrant.
Return crispy tofu to the pan, add 2 tbsp soy sauce, 1 tbsp calamansi/lemon juice, and 1 tbsp mayonnaise (optional). Toss well and serve.

title: Silky Tomato & Egg Stir-Fry
description: Sweet-savory jammy tomatoes folded into velvety scrambled eggs—one of the fastest comfort dishes over steamed rice.

substitutions.tomato: Canned diced tomatoes or 2 tbsp tomato ketchup mixed with water works in a pinch.

steps: Whisk 3 eggs with a pinch of salt. Cut 3 ripe tomatoes into wedges.
Heat 1 tbsp oil over medium-high heat. Pour in eggs, softly scramble into large curds for 45 seconds, and transfer to a plate.
Add another tsp of oil to the pan, sauté 2 cloves minced garlic, then add tomato wedges and stir-fry for 3 minutes until saucy.
Add a pinch of sugar and a splash of soy sauce or salt, return the eggs to the pan, and fold gently for 20 seconds.
